title: Carpet Padding Explained: Thickness, Density and Why It Matters More Than the Carpet
meta: Carpet padding explained: why 8 lb density beats extra thickness, which pad fits berber, plush and stairs, and what Edmonds homes need. From Wills Flooring.
keywords: carpet padding explained, carpet pad thickness and density, best carpet padding, 8 lb vs 6 lb carpet pad, rebond carpet pad, carpet pad for stairs, carpet installation Edmonds WA

blocks.lead: For most Edmonds bedrooms and living rooms, the right pad is a 7/16 in thick, 8 lb density rebond cushion. Density is what makes carpet last; thickness only makes it feel soft, and past 1/2 in it starts to hurt the carpet.
blocks.detail: Berber and looped carpets need a firmer, thinner pad, stairs need the firmest you can get, and carpet over a slab near the water should sit on a pad with a moisture barrier. Labor is $0.99 per sq ft whichever pad you pick, so upgrading it only moves the material line.

blocks.html: Carpet padding is the part of the job nobody sees and almost everyone under-buys. When we pull up a 15-year-old carpet in a Seaview or Westgate rambler, the carpet is often still intact; it is the pad that has turned to crumbs, and the carpet has been wearing against bare plywood for years. A common Reddit thread asks whether upgrading the pad is worth it or an upsell. It is worth it.

items.title: It absorbs the impact, not the carpet
items.text: Every footstep compresses the carpet fibers. With a good pad underneath, the pad takes most of that compression and springs back, so the fibers bend less and recover faster. Over a thin or worn pad, fibers crush against the subfloor and mat down in traffic lanes.

items.title: It quiets the room and the floor below
items.text: Pad is why carpeted upstairs bedrooms in a two-story Perrinville house are quieter than the hardwood downstairs. Denser pad blocks more footfall noise and helps condo owners in the Bowl meet building sound rules. A 5 lb pad does far less than an 8 lb one at the same thickness.

items.title: It insulates over cold floors
items.text: Over a slab, or over a crawlspace in a 1960s rambler, pad adds a real thermal break. Rebond and fiber pads trap air; rubber pads less so. If a room has always felt cold underfoot, the pad changes that more than the carpet fiber will.

items.title: It can stop spills from reaching the subfloor
items.text: Standard rebond is a sponge, so pet accidents soak into the plywood and come back as odor for years. A pad with a moisture barrier film on top keeps liquid where it can be extracted. Our damp marine air makes that more useful, not less, because wet subfloors dry slowly.

blocks.html: Labor is published and flat: $0.99 per sq ft stretched in over pad, $1.29 glue-down on a slab, $30 per step, $0.45 per sq ft to tear the old carpet and pad out. A 950 sq ft Westgate main floor with 14 stairs is 950 x ($0.99 + $0.45) + 14 x $30 = $1,788 in labor. Carpet and pad are quoted on top of that, and the pad upgrade is the cheapest line on the sheet.

blocks.text: The pad types you will be offered

items.html: Rebond (bonded urethane). The multicolored foam made from recycled cushion scraps, and the standard for good reason: durable, affordable, made in every density. 8 lb at 7/16 in is our default.

Frothed and memory foam. Denser, more uniform urethane. Frothed foam is very durable and thin; memory foam feels luxurious but is too soft under berber and slows carpet recovery. Fine in bedrooms, skip it on stairs.
Fiber pad (synthetic felt). Firm and flat, often 3/8 in. The right pad under berber, commercial loop and many wool carpets. It does not feel plush, which is the point.

Rubber (waffle or flat slab). Premium and long-lived. Flat rubber is excellent under wool and on stairs. Waffle rubber feels soft because of the air pockets and breaks down faster. Both are heavy to handle.
Moisture-barrier rebond. Regular rebond with a sealed film face. Our most common upgrade for homes with dogs and for slab rooms near the waterfront.

blocks.text: Match the pad to the carpet, not the other way around

items: 7/16 in rebond at 8 lb for family rooms and bedrooms

Keep it under 1/2 in so seams and stretch hold

b.tag: Loop pile: berber, level loop, many wools

blocks.text: Where Edmonds homes go wrong with pad

items.text: It looks fine, so the installer leaves it. Old pad has already lost its resilience where people walk, so new carpet inherits the old traffic lanes within a year. New carpet gets new pad, and the old pad goes out on the $0.45 per sq ft tear-out line.
A thick, cushy pad on a Seaview split-level staircase feels great for a month. Then the carpet loosens at the nosing and wrinkles. Stairs get a firm 8 lb pad or flat rubber.

items.d: Standard pad over a damp slab
items.text: Many 1950s to 1970s ramblers here have a slab family room that runs damp in winter. Ordinary rebond wicks that moisture up and smells within a season. Test the slab, then use a barrier pad or a glue-down install at $1.29 per sq ft.
Buildings in the Bowl and near the ferry often require a minimum sound rating for floor coverings. A dense pad is the cheapest way to meet it. Ask the HOA for the number first.

blocks.title: Do not judge pad by squeezing it:
blocks.text: The softest sample in the store is usually the lowest density and the first to fail. Turn it over, read the density in pounds, and pick 8 lb. We bring pad samples with the carpet samples to every carpet estimate so you can compare labels side by side.

faq.q: Is 8 lb carpet pad worth it over 6 lb?
faq.a: Yes for any room people walk through daily. An 8 lb pad keeps its bounce for the life of the carpet, while 6 lb pad flattens in traffic lanes and the carpet wears faster there. Labor is $0.99 per sq ft either way, so the upgrade costs only the difference in material.

Not past a point. Thickness adds softness, but carpet over pad thicker than 1/2 in flexes too much, stretches, and can wrinkle or pull at seams. Most warranties cap pad at 7/16 or 1/2 in. Choose density for durability and keep thickness at 7/16 in for cut pile, 3/8 in for loops.

faq.q: What is the best carpet pad for stairs?
faq.a: A firm, dense pad: 8 lb rebond at 3/8 to 7/16 in, or flat rubber. Stairs take the most concentrated wear in the house and a soft pad lets the carpet shift on the nosing. Stair labor is $30 per step and the pad should be fastened to each tread, not run loose down the flight.

faq.q: Do I need a moisture barrier pad?
faq.a: You need one if you have dogs or cats, small children, or a slab floor. The barrier keeps accidents on top of the pad where they can be blotted and extracted instead of soaking into the subfloor. In Edmonds homes with a damp lower level it also slows moisture from below.

faq.q: Can carpet pad be reused when installing new carpet?
faq.a: It should not be. Pad loses resilience exactly where people walked on the old carpet, so new carpet would sit on a floor that is already uneven. New carpet goes over new pad, and our $0.45 per sq ft tear-out line takes the old carpet and pad away together.

faq.q: What pad goes under berber carpet?
faq.a: A thin, firm one: 3/8 in at 8 lb density, or a fiber or flat rubber pad. Berber is a loop pile that stretches and ripples over soft, thick cushion, and many berber warranties require the thinner pad. For a softer step under a loop carpet, choose a denser pad rather than a thicker one.
